title: ICC prosecution to present 100 witnesses; protective measures may be implemented

blocks.text: The International Criminal Court (ICC) spokesperson on Tuesday said the prosecution team is expected to present over 100 witnesses during the trial of former president Rodrigo Duterte, with the tribunal possibly implementing protective measures for them.
Duterte’s trial is set to begin on November 30. In a statement to the media, ICC Spokesperson Oriane Maillet said this would be the first trial pertaining to a situation in the Philippines.

“The prosecution currently anticipates calling about 100 witnesses over the course of the trial, and after that, after the prosecution's case, the defense will have the opportunity to present its own evidence and its own witnesses,” Maillet said.
However, while 100 are expected to participate, Maillet said the court has authorized more than 500 victims to partake in the trial through legal representatives.

“The court also has a legal obligation to protect victims and witnesses, and depending on the circumstances of each individual, the judges may order protective measures to safeguard the security and the well-being of these witnesses,” Maillet said.
According to the ICC spokesperson, the exact duration of the trial will still depend on different factors, such as the number of witnesses and volume of evidence.
Maillet said the court has extensively prepared for Duterte’s trial, noting that it has generated national and international public interest.
The ICC briefings can be followed in person or online. However, the judges may move to a private or closed session to protect confidential information.

“Let's be clear, the court's role is not to pursue any political objective. Rather, it's to determine through independent and impartial judicial proceedings whether the charges have been proven according to the law. A fair trial is a fundamental principle of the Rome Statute,” Maillet said.
“Mr. Duterte is presumed innocent, unless and until proven guilty before the court,” she added.
With Duterte’s trial set to open on November 30, Joanna Korner is set to return as the Presiding Judge, alongside Judge Keebong Paek and Judge Nicolas Guillou.
The judges will first check if Duterte understands the charges being lodged against him and then he will enter a plea.
Maillet said that after this, the prosecution and legal representatives of victims will deliver opening statements. The defense’s opening statement will be heard later on in the trial.

“Following these opening statements, the testimony of the prosecution's first witness is expected to begin. Following that, the first five prosecution witnesses are expected to testify before the winter judicial recess, starting on the 18th of December,” Maillet said. — BAP, GMA News
